question.text: Godavari Opportunities AIF (Cat II, closed-ended). Called-up Capital INR 80 crore, Hurdle Rate 9% (compounded annually), fund has completed 3 full years with NAV tracked on a 'reference hurdle NAV' basis (starting at committed capital). What is the Reference Hurdle NAV at the end of Year 3?

explanation.text: The Logic: In a closed-ended Cat I/II fund, Hurdle NAV COMPOUNDS year over year. Year 3 Hurdle NAV = INR 80 crore x (1.09)^3 = INR 80 x 1.295029 = INR 103.60 crore (rounded to INR 103.59 crore). The chapter stresses the hurdle is a COMPOUND rate, not a simple rate. The Trap: A is simple interest: INR 80 x (1 + 3 x 0.09) = INR 101.60 crore; C and D are mis-compounded (wrong rate or periodicity). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same compound-hurdle principle. Private-market hurdles compound; hedge-fund HWMs in Cat III crystallise differently (high-water-mark-based) — XIX-E territory. Manager's Pro-Tip: When running LP distribution models, always label the hurdle 'compounded annually' explicitly in the PPM — ambiguity between simple/compound has caused real disputes at distribution time in Indian funds.
